title: Fractional parametric resonance in spintronic diodes
authors: Andrea Grimaldi, Denys Slobodianiuk, Eleonora Raimondo, Raghav Sharma, Anna Giordano, Mario Carpentieri, Hyunsoo Yang, Riccardo Tomasello, Roman Verba, Giovanni Finocchio
abstract: Parametric pumping is a powerful tool for the excitation, amplification, and processing of oscillations and waves of different nature. In general, parametric resonance can occur when the pumping frequency $f_p$ and eigenfrequency of a linear mode (or wave) $f_0$ satisfy the relation $f_p$=2$f_0$/n (n=1,2,3,...). While such parametric resonance is well known in mechanical, superconductive, and quantum systems, in magnetic and spintronic systems only the lowest (n=1) parametric resonance at double the spin wave mode frequency $f_p$=2$f_0$ was thoroughly studied and explored. Here, using a theoretical analysis based on both micromagnetic simulations and an analytical model, we show the emergence of resonances at fractional frequencies $f_p$=2$f_0$/n (with n>10) in spintronic diodes driven by the simultaneous action of ac spin-transfer torque (STT, current densities < $10^6$ A/cm2) and voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA, effective anisotropy fields < 50 mT). The analytical model shows that parametric magnetization dynamics is irreducible to the standard Mathieu model of a parametric oscillator and demonstrates the crucial role of VCMA-driven mode frequency modulation: together with parametric coupling, it results in higher-order odd (n=3,5,7,...) fractional resonances, observed above certain VCMA pumping threshold, while simultaneous action with linear STT drive produces thresholdless even (n=4,6,8,...) resonances. This higher-order parametric dynamics is not restricted to VCMA pumping and opens new directions for the application of spintronic diodes for nonlinear signal processing and electromagnetic energy harvesting.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes fractional parametric resonance in spintronic diodes subjected to combined STT and VCMA driving. It proves that higher-order resonances ($n>1$) exist, distinguishing between threshold-dependent odd resonances (VCMA only) and thresholdless even resonances (STT + VCMA). The findings establish a general framework for using these devices in nonlinear signal processing applications.
main_problem: The research investigates fractional parametric resonance in spintronic diodes, extending beyond the traditionally studied lowest-order ($n=1$) resonance.
main_result: The study demonstrates higher-order odd and even fractional resonances, showing that VCMA-driven modulation is crucial for these effects, opening avenues for nonlinear signal processing.
method: A theoretical analysis combining micromagnetic simulations with an analytical model was employed to characterize the magnetization dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is a spintronic diode (MTJ) driven by simultaneous ac Spin-Transfer Torque (STT) and Voltage-Controlled Magnetic Anisotropy (VCMA). The dynamics are modeled using equations derived from spin wave perturbation formalism, showing irreducibility to the standard Mathieu model.
key_observables: Resonance spectra, peak amplitudes in odd vs. even zones, threshold behavior, and broadband response.
important_parameters: STT current densities ($< 10^6$ A/cm$^2$), VCMA anisotropy fields ($< 50$ mT), and the resonance order $n$.
main_assumptions: The standard Mathieu model is insufficient for describing the full parametric magnetization dynamics; a more complete theoretical framework incorporating VCMA modulation is necessary.
figures_summary: Figures compare theoretical predictions to micromagnetic simulations, illustrating resonance spectra in both odd and even zones under varying external fields ($\mathbf{B}_{ext}$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by analyzing the dynamic equation governing magnetization amplitude, comparing results against numerical simulations, and concluding with a general framework for engineering these resonances.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the underlying physics involves parametric excitation in nonlinear oscillators (the magnetic system), which shares mathematical parallels with driven quantum systems studied in AMO/Quantum Optics.
